I bought this fragrance right at the introduction in 2010. I was looking for a special fragrance, researched online and found this recommendation of a "brand new" niche scent. I went to the only store in town which sold it, one of the biggest shopping houses in europe. No one knew Aventus back then and barely did people knew about Creed. 

I smelled the frangrance and fell in love. To this very day, I have never ever smelled a better thing like this first bottles of Aventus. It is really by far the most heavenly smell on earth.

I got compliments for left and right. In public office buildings in elevators, where never strangers start to talk, someone said "who is smelling so good" and a chatter about it started. On the street people stopped me: "Is this you, wow you smell so good!". Women, men, adults, older people. It was crazy. It was unbelievable.

I received so many compliments, one day in an office I worked the boss came over and asked us: "Who is smelling so good, the whole office smells so good!" I knew it was me, had only sprayed two times. I told him and in the middle of work he went to the store and came back with Creed Aventus.

Then the reformulations started: first, the Birch note was nearly completely vanished. By this time, many people started to buy this fragrance which was a real weapon. There is a reason people called it panty dropper. It really was. Why should there be so many people calling it like this if there never was something to it? It was. It just changed by the time the real masses adopted the fragrance.

It felt like Creed thought that this fragrance was too good to be on the market. At first I thought they will bring the real formula back for a higher price. Which would be ok, I would pay easily 1000$ on a bottle if it were the real formula. I thought they will do this, to outprice the masses and make it a niche again. But instead they just reformulated it so bad, that not only the smokiness was gone but later the lasting of the fragrance was dropped to half an hour. While it was days at the beginning.

If they ever will bring back the original frangrance, people who now don't understand the batch discussions, will understand.

I would both agree and disagree that this is the Rolex Submariner of the fragrance world. In terms of it's pricing it's pretty much spot on with the Sub; over what any non-enthusiast would consider a reasonable price but more so on the entry level for people that are really into fragrances or watches respectively. It's very iconic and anyone that knows a thing or two about the watch/fragrance world will probably recognize these two instantly. They are also both part of the casual/sports craze going on in the luxury world as of late. The same way a Submariner is a more casual piece made of non-precious metals, Creed Aventus is a sweet, leathery, citrusy and musky scent that isn't in your face like you might expect from a luxury perfume, but is a classic masterpiece regardless. Both feel at home wearing a suit, leather jacket or even a white shirt with jeans, but you get the point. Where I think this differs is that this is more of a niche fragrance wheras Rolex is pretty much known by everybody. This is usually where I run into trouble with these types of comparisons as well though, because Rolex is kind of in a unique situation. It is perceived by many to be the best watchmaker despite being outclassed by many others. In the car world we would say that Rolex is Ferrari in terms of public perception but in reality a much better comparison would be between Ferrari and Patek. Rolex is more like BMW or Porsche, though no one things BMW's are the 'best' cars ever made the same way many do with Rolex. Anyways, that's my two cents on it. Being a 'niche' fragrance house that pretty much everyone who knows anything about perfumes knows about, I'd compare Creed as a company more so to Richard Mille than Rolex. The prices don't line up though seeing as RM are literally skyrocketing in value.
